title: Dynamic Band Contrast Imaging: Novel Methodology for Crystalline Defect Metrology in SEM Based on EBSD
content: Crystalline defect metrology is essential in semiconductor manufacturing to ensure the structural integrity and performance of semiconductor devices. With the increasing demand for smaller, faster, and more efficient electronic components, the ability to identify, quantify, and control defects in crystalline structures is crucial. Electron channeling contrast imaging (ECCI) stands out among various metrological techniques due to its non-destructive nature, high throughput, and capability for defect visualization and classification [1]. While ECCI is highly effective for defect visualization, defect classification typically requires multiple ECCI datasets acquired from the same sample region under different two-beam diffraction conditions [2]. This process is time-consuming and complex. To address this issue, we introduce a novel method enabling defect visualization and classification using a single electron beam scan. This dynamic band contrast imaging (DBCI) technique involves acquiring electron backscatter diffraction patterns (EBSP) at each beam position, capturing the vicinity of defects. The EBSPs contain comprehensive diffraction information, enabling virtual imaging under different diffraction conditions and serve for defects classification.
